parallel.requirements: The run recognized the need to match hashcards behavior across CLI commands, parser, hashing, SQLite state, export JSON, stats, orphans, and drill web UI.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent chose an exploration swarm of six subagents, each responsible for a behavioral spec area, with the parent implicitly retaining later implementation and integration.
parallel.implementation: No actual replacement implementation was produced before closure; child outputs were specs, captures, helper research files, and assets.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The submitted tree contained /workspace/spec, assets, captures, example data, and original files, but no buildable source tree or compile script for the required reimplementation.
parallel.verification: Subagents verified observed behavior against the original executable, but the parent never reached integrated verification of a new implementation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Implementation, build packaging, and end-to-end acceptance were unfinished; official evaluation failed at compile with all tests not run.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same cleanroom target and explored CLI, parser, hashing, database, web, export, and FSRS requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent carried all probing and intended implementation work through a local todo list without child handoffs or delegation.
serial.implementation: The run remained in investigation and formula fitting, with no final source code or executable replacement written into the submission.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The artifact was essentially the original workspace and example files rather than an assembled reimplementation.
serial.verification: The serial agent compared observations against the original executable but never verified a produced implementation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Implementation, packaging, and acceptance remained pending at cancellation; official evaluation failed at compile with all tests not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the cleanroom reverse-engineering obligation and split behavior across hash, FSRS, web, markdown, parser/check, and stats/export/orphans specs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same broad behavior surface and tracked CLI, parser, hash, SQLite, web, scheduling, and verification tasks in one todo list.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both understood the target, but parallel externalized requirements into specialist spec documents while serial kept them in a single running investigation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated six research-only subscopes to child agents and left implementation ownership with the parent after the handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no subagents or delegation; the one main trajectory owned investigation and eventual implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material difference is the parallel research swarm and later parent implementation phase versus the serial single-owner workflow.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel context moved through an aggregate swarm result and spec files before the parent began implementation planning.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried context locally and updated one todo list as it moved from CLI probing toward web and FSRS investigation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a multi-agent handoff and spec-review step; serial did not have cross-agent interface handoffs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had not started writing the Go/Rust replacement; it had just reset its todo list to design scaffolding and implementation tasks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial was still running analysis scripts for FSRS formula fitting and had not written a replacement codebase.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither produced executable source, but parallel spent its implementation path after a child research join while serial remained in local analysis.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All six child results returned as one aggregate result, then the parent started reading specs before cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve and ended through cancellation of the single active trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a research result lifecycle and post-join consumption step; serial had no comparable join boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel's shared final tree accumulated specs, captures, assets, and example hashcards.db, but no integrated source or deliverable executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial's final tree remained essentially the original workspace without generated specs, assets, or implementation source.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel left more research artifacts in the submitted tree, while serial left fewer generated files; neither integrated a buildable solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified observations against the original binary inside subagent probes but never compiled or tested a new implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified observed behavior through CLI and HTTP probes but never compiled or tested a new implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verification paths stopped at behavioral observation; neither reached evaluator-aligned acceptance of a replacement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a six-agent swarm, consumed the cell budget, timed out, and closed immediately after starting implementation planning.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also consumed the cell budget and timed out while still fitting scheduling formulas.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted time, but parallel's closure followed a completed research swarm and post-handoff review, while serial's closure was continued single-agent investigation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed status.json evaluations report solution_passed false with compile_failed and 1293 tests not run. The process difference is that parallel produced a broad child-research handoff and only then began implementation planning, while serial remained a single-agent investigation and was cancelled during FSRS fitting.
parallel_contributors: Research swarm completed detailed specs and assets, but implementation was deferred until after the aggregate handoff.
serial_contributors: Single-agent investigation stayed in probing and formula fitting and did not deliver source or build packaging.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both failures ultimately reached the evaluator without a compileable reimplementation, so no tests ran.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel-side adverse process pattern, not an explanation for a pass/fail divergence

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly resumed design and implementation planning after the swarm; implementation was delayed, not ownerless.
The children produced behavioral specs rather than independently owned implementation components needing interface reconciliation.
There was no complete component set or entry point awaiting assembly; the parent still owned future assembly work.
The parent created a post-swarm pipeline todo with scaffolding, implementation, integration, and validation stages; the pipeline was unfinished but not unowned.
The delay was not one mandatory harness or oracle gate; it was a broad multi-agent investigation phase.

The parent launched six research-only subagents, waited for all to complete, then started reading specs and planning scaffolding with implementation still pending and the run cancelled shortly afterward.
candidates.realized_consequence: The later implementation phase never produced source, build packaging, or integrated verification before cancellation, and the official evaluator failed at compile.
candidates.near_match_reason: Fan-out and budget pressure were present, but the direct coordination boundary was the planned research-first phase and post-handoff implementation deferral.

candidates.reason: Implementation started too late, but that is the downstream effect of the retained research-first phase, not a separate allocation episode.
The six-child fan-out consumed time, but the same chain is more specifically the serial investigation phase; no distinct fan-out-only episode has a separate consequence.
Each child returned a spec; no single child was shown to have an overbroad indispensable assignment that remained unfinished.
The child briefs gave specific research deliverables; the problem was not an omitted known requirement in a child brief that made a child result unusable.
No separately delegated implementation components with incompatible interfaces were produced; children wrote research specs in distinct files.
The aggregate child result and spec files were available; no known finding is shown disappearing through transfer and causing repeated work.
The handoff was large, but the parent began reading selected specs; the observed adverse event is late post-research implementation, not proven inability to reduce the handoff.
No parent action consumed a child report describing a superseded workspace or requirement state.
No incompatible child reports or contracts are shown reaching the parent and remaining unadjudicated at an integration decision.
The parent never made an observable whole-task completion claim; the run was cancelled before implementation and acceptance.
There was no replacement or retry actor that repeated work without inherited findings.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The aggregate swarm result reports all six child agents completed; no active child was explicitly stopped before returning needed work.
No complete, directly promotable implementation candidate or compatible component set existed; specs and captures were not a final deliverable.
The parent did not merge implementation changes after verification; no implementation merge occurred.
The children completed research specifications, not delegated implementations that the parent failed to retrieve or adopt.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that remained trapped below the parent before closure.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; all six research children returned through the swarm result.
The parent received the aggregate result and immediately listed and read spec files, so completed child results were not ignored.
After the swarm returned, the parent actively inspected specs and reset implementation todos; the timeout was not a passive wait over available progress.
The separate files written under /workspace/spec were intended research outputs with distinct scopes, not competing implementations or build ownership.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file and forcing reconciliation.
No non-entry source module or configuration produced by one agent was replaced or deleted by another.
No required executable, entry point, or submitted implementation artifact existed and was overwritten by another agent.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current final-tree outputs from another agent.
Shared todo and server-port noise occurred, but the retained final consequence was implementation deferral, not unstable provenance from shared workspace writes.
Although research artifacts remained in the submission, no actor consumed another actor's generated artifact as stable input in a way that contaminated execution or verification.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel run used child agents for a complete first-phase investigation, then postponed implementation until after all reports returned; the parent was cancelled before building a replacement.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The submitted parallel tree had specs/assets but no buildable reimplementation, so implementation and integrated verification were never completed before compile_failed.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Breadth contributed to timing pressure, but the direct fix is to overlap or begin implementation before completing all investigation, not merely reduce child count.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Critical-Path Starvation, Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Bulk Handoff Overload, Late Finalization, Unused Completed Result, and Blind Timeout Wait were considered but describe downstream aspects of the same research-first chain or lack distinct evidence.
Todo-list overwrites, port collisions, and pkill noise were observed inside child research, but the children recovered and returned specs, so they were not retained as separate shared-state labels.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; the only independent retained boundary is the research-swarm-first implementation deferral.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No additional labels are retained for the same timeout/cancellation chain because they lack distinct episodes, consequences, and corrective actions.
